facts.label: Dias da semana
facts.sub: Para dias use on: on Monday, on Friday. Para horas use at: at six. Dias da semana começam com letra maiúscula em inglês.

facts.label: on para dias, at para horas
facts.sub: Para dias, use “on”: on Monday, on Friday. Para horas, use “at”: at six. Para meses, “in”: in June. Os dias da semana e os meses sempre começam com letra maiúscula em inglês, ao contrário do português.

facts.label: Calendários americanos
facts.sub: Em muitos calendários dos EUA a semana começa no domingo, e não na segunda. Datas costumam ser escritas mês, dia, ano. Por isso, ao marcar um compromisso, confirme com o dia da semana: “Is that Friday the 12th?”.

compare.br: In Portuguese, most days end in “-feira” and are written in lowercase, like segunda-feira.
compare.us: In English, each day has its own name, written with a capital letter: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday…
compare.tip: Use on + day (on Friday), at + time (at six) and in + part of the day (in the evening).

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Days of the week start with a capital letter in English.
items.why: We write Monday, Friday, Sunday, not monday.

items.s: Sunday is named after the Sun.
The word Thursday comes from the Roman god Jupiter.
items.why: Thursday comes from Thor, the Norse god of thunder. (Latin had Jupiter’s day, and Thor is the Norse match for Jupiter.)

pages.title: My week in San Francisco · 1/3
paragraphs: I live in San Francisco, a city with steep hills and a red bridge called the Golden Gate. It opened in 1937. Today my friend Nina asks me, “**What day is it today?**” “**It’s Monday**,” I say.

“**Oh no!** **I have class on Mondays**,” says Nina. “**When do you have class?**” I ask. “**On Monday and Wednesday**,” she says. I have yoga on **Friday**. “Come with me!” I tell her. “**Great! What time?**” she asks. “**At six in the evening**,” I say. “**See you on Friday!**”

pages.title: My week in San Francisco · 2/3
paragraphs: I like Fridays, but many people do not like Mondays. In 1979, an Irish band, The Boomtown Rats, made a song called “I Don’t Like Mondays”. It was a big hit in the United Kingdom. Today the title is a common phrase for people who find the start of the week hard.
Here is my week. On Monday I study. On Tuesday I work. On Wednesday I walk by the sea. On Thursday I cook. On Friday I do yoga. On the **weekend**, I rest, see friends and sometimes ride a cable car.

pages.focus: ligação: is it (i-zit) e you on (you-on)
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: Em perguntas curtas como “What day is it today?”, as palavras pequenas se grudam: “is it” vira “i-zit”. Se você separar demais, a frase perde o ritmo do inglês.
pages.how: Una o /s/ de is, que vira /z/, ao it: i·zit. Una you e on sem pausa: you·on. Dê força aos dias da semana (MON-day, FRI-day) e deixe as palavras pequenas leves e rápidas.
pages.tip: Os dias terminam em -day, pronunciado “dei”, com a força na primeira sílaba, menos em Wednesday: WENZ-day.
